scope: development tooling: exact worker-wrapper identity predicate for supervisor capacity scanning and launch recovery

source.delivery_head_binding: The governed handoff freezes the PR head containing this manifest; implementation_commit is its source ancestor.

problem.summary: Two independent live audits found the scheduler identified a live worker_runner.py wrapper with a raw substring search ("worker_runner.py" in the whole /proc/<pid>/cmdline text) instead of an exact argv-path predicate. Provider CLI and bwrap sandbox descendants inherit the wake prompt as an argv value; when that inherited prompt text itself contains the literal string "worker_runner.py" (for example while quoting the task's own artifact path), the substring search matched the descendant too. The scheduler reported six active processes while the watchdog's exact predicate (supervisor_watchdog.cmdline_is_worker_runner) correctly identified three real wrappers, so the global planner could believe genuinely free capacity slots were occupied.

fix.predicate: supervisor.py now imports and reuses supervisor_watchdog.cmdline_is_worker_runner at both identity call sites instead of keeping separate, drifted substring checks. The predicate NUL-splits /proc/<pid>/cmdline into real argv tokens and requires one of the first four tokens to be path-shaped (starts with '/' or '.', no whitespace), have Path(token).name == 'worker_runner.py', and have '.orchestrator' in Path(token).parts.
unchanged: zombie/dead-process filtering (Z/X state check, pid_is_alive gate)
PID start-tick / process-generation checks and fail-closed RuntimeError on unreadable evidence
run-id handling, lease behavior, promotion-drain behavior
max_concurrent_workers capacity ceiling (not raised; this task corrects identity, not the limit)

acceptance_evidence.exact_predicate: Both scan_live_worker_pids_by_agent and _proc_worker_runner_launch_marker now call the single shared supervisor_watchdog.cmdline_is_worker_runner predicate; no separate substring check remains at either site.
acceptance_evidence.focused_regressions: test_scan_live_worker_pids_excludes_prompt_text_and_bwrap_descendants proves a real .orchestrator/worker_runner.py wrapper is counted exactly once (live_pids == {"Codex": [900001]}) while a bwrap descendant and a provider-CLI descendant that both carry the same wake prompt (one quoting the literal text 'worker_runner.py') are excluded. test_proc_worker_runner_launch_marker_rejects_prompt_text_match proves the same rejection for launch-recovery identity even when ORCH_TASK_ID/ORCH_AGENT_ID match.
acceptance_evidence.preserved_behavior: Pre-existing test_zombie_worker_pid_treated_as_non_live_and_does_not_block_dispatch continues to pass unchanged; full .orchestrator/test_supervisor.py and .orchestrator/test_supervisor_watchdog.py suites pass with no regressions.
acceptance_evidence.documentation: docs/operations/supervisor-worker-identity.md records the identity rule, its procfs boundaries, the relation between watchdog and scheduler counts, and a read-only runtime health/count observation.
acceptance_evidence.delivery_scope: Only the declared tooling files (.orchestrator/supervisor.py, .orchestrator/test_supervisor.py, docs/operations/supervisor-worker-identity.md, this evidence file) changed; no product runtime behavior, hosted deployment, external branch protection, task state, or unrelated worktree was touched.

live_activation.note: This task changes only the source tree. Runtime activation on a live supervisor is a separate governed promotion (scripts/promote_supervisor_runtime.py) after this source merges into dev.
live_activation.observed_note: The running supervisor's dispatch_runtime.source_sha predates this fix, so its live process image still runs the prior substring-based scan until an operator promotes the merged commit.
